changes: Of the 136 changed records, 42 are for crates added by the work since 0.1.5 before the lock refresh (dependants not traced), 5 for crates added by the refresh (const-oid-0.10.3, constant_time_eq-0.6.1, hybrid-array-0.4.15, utf_types-1.0.0, zeroize_derive-1.5.0), and 89 are new versions of crates already present.
The whole lock was refreshed for RUSTSEC advisories. Direct pins: rmcp 3.10.0, naga 30.0.2, zip 9.5.1.

zip 9.0.0 is updated to 9.5.1. Its locked dependencies go from 6 to 12: added constant_time_eq, getrandom, libc, nix, windows-sys, zeroize; removed none. Its LICENSE has sha256 58545fed1565e42d687aecec6897d35c6d37ccb71479a137c0deb2203e125c79, the same as the 9.0.0 text recorded for 0.1.5 (58545fed1565e42d687aecec6897d35c6d37ccb71479a137c0deb2203e125c79). NOH's use of the crate was not re-examined for this record.

Six notice supplements are added for crates published without a licence file: clipboard-win-5.4.3, fdsm-0.8.0, fdsm-ttf-parser-0.2.0, harfrust-0.5.2, objc2-0.5.3, objc2-0.6.5. Each pins the upstream repository, the commit recorded in the crate's .cargo_vcs_info.json, and the file's Git blob and SHA-256.
tools/rust_notices.py accepts gitlab.com as well as github.com as the forge of a supplement (fdsm is hosted on GitLab); the pinned-commit rule is unchanged.

Left in place, ignored by the generator: 23 of the 81 notice supplements and 13 of the 14 declared-licence supplements are for versions no longer locked (only dispatch-0.2.0 remains in use among the latter).
The syllable dictionaries are new inputs: assets/syllable-sources.lock.json pins the two public datasets and tools/build_syllable_dicts.py builds the dictionaries from them.

The hashes of the native, speech and standard-library-source inputs are unchanged from the 0.1.5 record: LICENSE, assets/delivery-windows.lock.json, assets/preview-runtime.json, assets/speech-bundle.json, assets/windows-native.lock.json, rust_standard_library_source, tools/windows_runtime.py.

The statements on Windows native sources, native notices and CUDA terms remain those of docs/WINDOWS_0_1_5_INPUTS.md: the hashes of assets/delivery-windows.lock.json, assets/preview-runtime.json, assets/windows-native.lock.json and tools/windows_runtime.py equal those of the 0.1.5 record.

licence_reading.method: A script, not part of the repository's tools, run on the vendored sources and on the pinned supplement texts. In the files the notice generator selects as notice files, it recognises 17 licence texts by one characteristic sentence each. For an OR expression one recognised alternative is enough; for AND every named licence must be recognised.
limits: Recognition by sentence, not a word-by-word comparison with canonical texts.
Source headers, READMEs and files not selected as notice files are not read; a file holding a recognised text plus other terms passes.
Which crates are compiled into this platform's binary was not determined; the records cover the whole locked graph.

objc2-0.6.5.script_remark: unrecognised text: LICENSE.md (1339 bytes); no text matches a declared licence
objc2-0.6.5.reading: The pinned LICENSE.md is the project's licensing explanation with links, not an MIT text. It is byte-identical to the file recorded for objc2 0.6.4 in 0.1.5 (sha256 7f976f7e9cb2d87df7230606feb932c3f21ac0e664045a775b600046ff850c54). The crate declares MIT and no MIT text with its copyright line is shipped for it; the same was true of 0.6.4 in 0.1.5, which is a fact and not a clearance. macOS is not a published platform (the delivery policy lists 2 unresolved redistribution gaps for macos-arm64, so the pipeline refuses it); as far as target gating goes, not verified by a build, this crate reaches users only through the vendored source archive. OPEN POINT for the maintainer: add a declared-licence supplement, or accept as is.
